tooltip.title: Treatment of Prurigo Nodularis (PN)
tooltip.markdown: The goal is to break the vicious itch-scratch cycle. Management requires a multimodal approach targeting the intense itch and the resulting skin lesions.

tooltip.title: First-Line Therapies for PN
tooltip.markdown: Focus on potent anti-inflammatory and antipruritic topicals.

tooltip.title: High-Potency Topical Steroids
tooltip.markdown: Often used under occlusion (e.g., Unna boot) or as a medicated tape (flurandrenolide) to enhance penetration and provide a physical barrier to scratching.

tooltip.title: Intralesional Corticosteroids
tooltip.markdown: Direct injection of triamcinolone into nodules is effective for alleviating pruritus and flattening lesions.

tooltip.title: Supportive Topicals
tooltip.markdown: Topical anesthetics (pramoxine) and cooling agents (menthol) provide symptomatic relief.

tooltip.title: Second-Line Therapies for PN
tooltip.markdown: For patients with widespread or refractory disease.

tooltip.title: Phototherapy
tooltip.markdown: Narrowband UVB (NBUVB) is a useful option for generalized PN.

tooltip.title: Gabapentinoids
tooltip.markdown: Gabapentin and pregabalin are first-line systemic agents for targeting the neuropathic component of PN itch.

tooltip.title: Systemic Immunomodulators
tooltip.markdown: Agents like methotrexate, cyclosporine, and dupilumab are used for their potent anti-inflammatory and antipruritic effects.

tooltip.title: Nemolizumab (Nemluvio)
tooltip.markdown: FDA-approved monoclonal antibody targeting IL-31 receptor alpha. First-in-class biologic specifically approved for prurigo nodularis, demonstrating significant itch reduction and lesion improvement.

tooltip.title: Opioid Modulators
tooltip.markdown: Opioid antagonists like naltrexone can be effective.

tooltip.title: Thalidomide
tooltip.markdown: A neuroactive medication reserved for patients who have failed traditional therapies due to its significant side effect profile.

tooltip.title: Other Emerging Targeted Therapies
tooltip.markdown: Additional biologics and small molecules in development, including serlopitant (NK1R inhibitor) and other novel agents targeting itch pathways.
